newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says no buyers for Food Terminal.
newsitem.headline: Manila says no buyers for Food Terminal.

text.p: The Philippine government failed on Wednesday to attract bidders for the privatisation of Food Terminal Inc, a 121-hectare agro-industrial complex at the edge of the Manila's Makati financial district.
"I hereby declare a failed bidding because there were no bids submitted," Agriculture Undersecretary Marinela Castillo said during the auction.
Castillo said interested bidders such as the groups of Filinvest Development Corp and Metro Pacific Corp sent letters yesterday informing the government they were not going to bid.
"The privatisation of FTI does not conform with their corporate plans," Castillo said when asked as to why the qualified bidders decided to withdraw from the auction.
On Tuesday, another qualified bidder, Keppel Corp Ltd, also announced in Singapore that it was not participating in the bidding process after re-examining the project's feasibility.
The government was selling 51 percent of Food Terminal Inc for at least 6.97 billion pesos.

Food Terminal president Romeo David told Reuters interested buyers might have been discouraged by one of the contract provisions which required three-fourth of the vote on any major decision regarding the terminal complex.

The terminal was incorporated in 1968 to stabilise prices of commodities in Manila through an efficient agriculture marketing system. But deterioration of stocks and high interest costs eventually resulted in huge losses for the complex.
